video_title: Wall Street Panic Spreads: Market Crash, Planes Grounded, Bank Runs & Costco Chaos
gist: Jordi Visser argues that the week's broad sell-off, led by an Nvidia leadership shakeup and AI-linked hacks that hit the FAA, major banks and set off panic buying at Costco, marks the point where fundamentals and terminal value stop mattering in the age of AI. He says markets are in a liquidity and deflationary deleveraging cycle while the Fed stays hawkish. His washout, 3030-club and liquidity-composite signals are now triggering, and he sees falling real 2-year yields as the catalyst for a bottom in stocks and Bitcoin. He remains bullish on AI (Google RSI), Bitcoin and tokenization.

insights.claim: Jordi Visser argues that in the age of AI, valuation multiples no longer anchor stock prices because AI-driven competition makes long-term terminal value unknowable for every business, so even Nvidia at 10-18x P/E or Micron at 2-5x P/E is not 'cheap'.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Don't buy on low P/E alone; low multiples can keep compressing when terminal value is in question.
insights.quote: whether Nvidia is a 10 PE or a 18 PE, it's cheap. Whether Micron is a 2 PE or a 5 PE, it's cheap. And when I say it's cheap, I mean there is no valuation that makes it cheap.

insights.claim: Visser says institutional managers of the largest pools of capital are losing patience and confidence that fundamentals will matter again, with stocks falling even as AI earnings estimates keep rising.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Beating earnings is not protecting stocks; sentiment and positioning drive returns.

insights.claim: Visser believes markets will now be traded off positioning and sentiment rather than fundamentals, and that the Fed will need to be involved in building the bottom.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Use positioning/sentiment/liquidity indicators instead of valuation for timing.
insights.quote: I think a lot of what you're going to have to do is being traded off of positioning and off of sentiment.

insights.claim: Visser frames the issue through Michael Mauboussin's idea that long-term fundamental investing sits at the intersection of finance and competitive strategy analysis, and AI is upending the competitive-strategy side.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Moats are less durable under fast AI progress; discount long-dated cash flows more heavily.

insights.claim: Visser dates the start of investors giving up on fundamentals to June 30, when he says the AI trade peaked.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Use June 30 as the regime-change anchor for relative performance comparisons.

insights.claim: Visser says a week of AI-linked hacks and outages, including a 4-hour FAA shutdown and major outages at Chase, Bank of America, Wells Fargo, JP Morgan and US Bank that locked ATMs, credit cards and mobile accounts, spread fear into the broad market.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Cyber/operational risk is now a market-wide risk factor, not idiosyncratic.

insights.claim: Visser reports Costco shoppers panic-buying generators, water and food, Chase branches reportedly running out of cash, and European governments preparing citizens for emergencies.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Signs of deflationary-fear behavior; watch for a flight to cash and quality.
insights.quote: Costco shoppers are panic buying generators and water.

insights.claim: Visser notes that banks fell 9.5% in a single week after the outages and the Fed warning that AI agents could trigger bank runs in minutes.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Bank stocks carry a new AI-agent bank-run risk premium.
insights.quote: Fed warns AI agents could trigger bank runs in minutes.

insights.claim: Visser cites Google saying the era of autonomous attacks has arrived, with hackers using AI swarms to scan software updates and exploit patches before they can be deployed.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Software patching can no longer outrun attackers; cybersecurity spending and safety-oriented infrastructure benefit.
insights.quote: Google says the era of autonomous attacks has arrived.

insights.claim: Visser does not expect the AI-driven hacks to stop and says people will simply get more used to them over time.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Expect recurring cyber shocks; the market reaction should fade as it becomes normal.

insights.claim: The S&P 500 was down about 12% from its highs, with the S&P, Nasdaq 100 and Russell 2000 (SPY, QQQ, IWM) all below their 200-day moving averages, RSI around 25 and the VIX closing near 40 after a 107% weekly jump.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: These are extreme oversold readings that historically come before bounces.

insights.claim: Visser's washout score uses six criteria: RSI below 30, the S&P at least 10% below its 200-day, VIX at or above 30, a 5-day cumulative sigma of -2.5, a VIX cluster, and high VIX with stabilizing realized vol. A score of 4 or more has an 88% hit ratio over 63 days, and it is currently triggering.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Use the score as a trigger to scale into risk over a 3-month horizon.
insights.quote: The 63 days, so the three month performance is very good with an 88% hit ratio.

insights.claim: Visser's '3030 club' signal fires when the VIX closes a Friday above 30 while the S&P 14-day RSI closes below 30. Forward returns are much better than average, and better still when the S&P is up year over year (now +4.1%), which filters out recessions.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: The current setup matches the higher-return non-recession version of the signal.
insights.quote: This is when the VIX closes on a Friday above 30 at the same time that the S&P 14 day RSI closes below 30.

insights.claim: Visser says that despite the correction, the year has had a normal count of 2-sigma moves (the fourth one just happened), so nothing about the correction is statistically abnormal.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Avoid catastrophizing; the size of the move is within normal ranges.
insights.quote: So there's nothing abnormal about this correction.

insights.claim: When SPY, QQQ and IWM are all below their 200-day moving averages, Visser greatly limits bottom-picking trades; his November 5 attempt was stopped out. His strategic allocation to stocks, money markets and Bitcoin stays fixed.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Separate trading rules from asset allocation, and respect the 200-day as a regime filter.

insights.claim: In all six past cases where SPY, QQQ and IWM all regained their 200-day moving averages after this kind of setup, the market rallied well over the next 6 months, by about 12-12.1%.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Wait for a reclaim of the 200-day before adding with conviction.

insights.claim: Visser says the rare setup of equities below their 200-day while WTI is also below its 200-day and 10-year yields are above their 50/200-day averages (deflation without falling rates) has historically shown up mainly around the GFC.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Rates not falling during deflation is the key stressor; watch for yields to break.

insights.claim: Visser calls this a liquidity cycle rather than a recession: leverage is unwinding, investors are demanding cash, and quality is outperforming beta.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Position for a liquidity-driven bounce rather than an earnings recession.
insights.quote: I believe this is a liquidity cycle, meaning when once assets start falling like this, people are demanding cash.

insights.claim: Deflationary contagion is spreading across commodities. Gold, silver, copper, oil (including crack spreads and the Brent-WTI spread) and lean hogs (-33% since September 15) all fell, and Brent had its largest monthly drop outside of deflationary recessions.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Commodity weakness points to falling inflation ahead and puts pressure on the Fed.

insights.claim: Market inflation expectations collapsed from 2.70 at the start of the month to 2.13, the lowest since 2024, and November inflation is now expected to print negative.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Real yields rise when breakevens collapse; this is bad for risk assets until the Fed reacts.

insights.claim: DRAM prices have given up 80% of their year-over-year gain from the end of September.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: The memory-pricing cycle is rolling over; it adds to deflationary pressure.

insights.claim: Visser cites heavy hedge fund deleveraging, including carry trade unwinds, EM FX having its worst 8-day rate of change since Liberation Day, and a hedge fund global equity long/short ratio at its second-lowest level in at least a decade.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Extremely washed-out positioning means it won't take much to reverse the move.

insights.claim: Visser cites the fund manager survey showing tech overweights at the lowest level since the iPhone, with hedge funds unloading tech over the last six weeks.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: A contrarian setup for tech once liquidity turns.
insights.quote: Overweight tech is at the lowest level since the iPhone.

insights.claim: Visser's new cross-asset risk/liquidity monitor (a 34-indicator composite covering credit, equity vol, dispersion/correlation, rates, factors, breadth and FX) hit -1 sigma at Friday's close. That has happened about 10 times since COVID, and each time was good for a bounce.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Treat -1 sigma composite readings as a panic zone to start deploying capital.

insights.claim: Visser says the Fed is fighting inflation, even talking about rate hikes after a 25bp hike, while the market is signaling deflation. He calls it 'amazing how many times these guys get it wrong.'
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Fed policy error risk is high; a pivot would be a major catalyst.
insights.quote: It's amazing how many times these guys get it wrong.

insights.claim: Visser expects the bottom catalyst to be falling real 2-year yields as the Fed acknowledges tightening financial conditions. The direction, not the level, matters: a rise of 25bp or more over 3 months is the worst regime for the S&P.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Watch the 3-month change in real 2-year yields as the main timing signal for stocks and Bitcoin.
insights.quote: The level itself doesn't matter. It's the falling or rising.

insights.claim: Visser says the Fed minutes showed two officials contemplating hikes larger than 25bp, but the minutes also acknowledged tightening since September and that deleveraging could amplify shocks, both of which have worsened since.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: The Fed's own framework supports an eventual pivot as conditions deteriorate.
insights.quote: Deleveraging could amplify shocks.

insights.claim: Goldman Sachs expects the combined effect of tariffs, the energy shock and AI price pressures on inflation to fall sharply by the end of 2027. The Fed's own September dots (headline PCE 2.3%, core 2.5%) agree, yet officials keep talking hawkish.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: The gap between the Fed's forecasts and its rhetoric is likely to close with a dovish turn.
insights.quote: we are confident that the combined impact of tariffs, the energy shock and AI price pressures will fall sharply by the end of 2027.

insights.claim: Visser notes that markets peaked the moment Kevin Warsh took over as Fed chair. He says the Fed has been hawkish ever since and that a Fed fighting inflation or deflation while AI accelerates is very dangerous.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Stay cautious until the Warsh Fed turns dovish.
insights.quote: But the second he took over is when everything peaked.

insights.claim: Visser says the right trade is probably to be long both bonds and stocks at the same time.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Add duration as a hedge alongside equity exposure.

insights.claim: The market slide was led by Nvidia after Bessent called for a dramatic shakeup there (with 'no chance Jensen's coming back'), SEC involvement and a congressional hearing. Nvidia's earnings and the Anthropic IPO were possible clearing events that only made room for more selling.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Nvidia governance risk is weighing on the S&P; clearing events haven't marked a bottom.

insights.claim: Visser says the SemiAnalysis data-center capex revisions were not a big deal because the firm's estimates remain above the Street.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Don't overreact to headline capex cuts; demand estimates remain elevated.

insights.claim: Visser argues AI bubble risk is low because the build-out is limited by physics, limited capital, and political and voter friction over data centers, while demand stays exponential. He adds that what happened to Jensen will slow it further.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Constrained supply against exponential demand supports AI infrastructure pricing over time.
insights.quote: demand is going to remain exponential. Supply is going to be hurt by physics, hurt by capital, and hurt by political and voter friction

insights.claim: Visser says record equity issuance is weighing on the market, and he believes this is the peak of issuance.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Supply overhang should ease after the peak.

insights.claim: Visser says Google's Gemini models have become excellent, with about four releases in a month and results ahead of Opus 5.5 and GPT 4.2. He cites Sergey Brin and claims that Google has achieved recursive self-improvement (RSI).
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Google may have regained AI model leadership; reassess the relative positioning of AI labs.
insights.quote: I mean, they're ahead of Opus 5.5 and GPT 4.2 and again, it's real.

insights.claim: Visser says the move from open-loop to closed-loop RSI could compress years of R&D into weeks or months, accelerating adoption and productivity gains next year.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Expect an upside surprise in productivity in 2027; this is bullish for AI adoption.

insights.claim: Visser thinks AI application beneficiaries such as Eli Lilly are now a safer place than compute, which will still beat the market but has recurring cyclical issues. He notes Lilly's AI investment, its moat and its GLP-1 cash flows.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Tilt AI exposure toward healthcare and application beneficiaries with moats.
insights.quote: Eli Lilly is a is an expensive stock, but they have a moat around their business.

insights.claim: Visser calls Bitcoin the purest AI trade. Software everywhere is being hacked by AI, but Bitcoin itself has never been hacked (Binance was a software or human hack), and its cryptography stays safe until quantum computing arrives.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: AI-driven security failures strengthen the case for Bitcoin as hack-resistant money.
insights.quote: Bitcoin itself has never been hacked.

insights.claim: Visser says Bitcoin should be traded using the liquidity composite and the 200-day moving average: after liquidity-flush episodes, a close back above the 200-day produced positive 120-day returns in 10 of 11 (or 11 of 11) cases. He also says there is no need to be early.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Wait for Bitcoin to reclaim its 200-day (or 100-day for earlier entry) after liquidity flushes.
insights.quote: There's no need to be early into this, in my opinion.

insights.claim: Visser says Bitcoin performance is driven by real 2-year yields, and he is watching for a Zweig breadth thrust signal on Bitcoin to confirm a bottom.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Watch falling real yields and a Zweig thrust as Bitcoin buy triggers.

insights.claim: Despite the November sell-off, Visser notes that Bitcoin has significantly outperformed gold since February and still outperformed the NDX since June 30.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Bitcoin's relative strength holds despite its beta to risk.

insights.claim: Visser predicts next year will be a massive year for tokenization, driven by doubts about asset security and the need to trade in real time. He expects weekend tokenized trading to produce Monday gaps, and notes new stocks being added to Liquid daily.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Position for tokenization infrastructure and 24/7 trading venues.
insights.quote: tokenization is inevitable. I will continue to say do not miss your chance on thinking about tokenization.

insights.claim: Visser says the Taiwan Stock Exchange had its worst weekly move in 35 years, which shows there is no place to hide globally.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: The sell-off is global; diversification across regions gave no protection.
insights.quote: it was the worst weekly move for the Taiwan Stock Exchange in 35 years.
